questions.stem: A can complete a work in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. How many days will they take to complete it together?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/12/day; B's rate = 1/18/day. Combined = 1/12+1/18 = 3/36+2/36 = 5/36/day. Days together = 36/5 = 7.2 days. **Short Trick:** Formula: AB/(A+B) = 12×18/(12+18) = 216/30 = 7.2 days.

questions.stem: X is twice as efficient as Y. Together they finish a work in 14 days. In how many days can Y alone finish the work?
questions.explanation: B is correct. X is twice as efficient → X takes half the time of Y. Let Y take 'y' days; X takes 'y/2' days. Combined: 1/(y/2)+1/y = 2/y+1/y = 3/y = 1/14 → y = 42 days. Verify: X=21 days, Y=42 days; 1/21+1/42=2/42+1/42=3/42=1/14 ✓.

questions.stem: A and B together can do a work in 10 days. B alone can do it in 15 days. In how many days can A alone do it?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = Combined rate − B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30 per day. A alone takes 30 days. **Short Trick:** LCM(10,15)=30. Together=3 units/day; B=2 units/day; A=3−2=1 unit/day. A alone takes 30 days.

questions.stem: 15 men can finish a work in 20 days. In how many days can 25 men finish the same work?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total work = 15 men × 20 days = 300 man-days. With 25 men: days = 300/25 = 12 days. **Short Trick:** Men × Days = constant (inverse proportion). M₁D₁=M₂D₂ → 15×20=25×D₂ → D₂=12.

questions.stem: A and B together finish work in 6 days. A alone finishes it in 10 days. If B is paid ₹900 for his share of the work, what is A's wage?
questions.explanation: B is correct. B's rate = 1/6−1/10 = 5/30−3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Ratio of work done: A:B = 1/10 : 1/15 = 15:10 = 3:2. B's share = 2/5 of total wages. 2/5 × total = ₹900 → total = ₹2250. A's wage = 3/5 × ₹2250 = ₹1350. **Rule:** In work-pay problems, wages are always split in ratio of work rates.

questions.stem: P can do a work in 24 days. Q is 50% more efficient than P. In how many days will Q finish the work?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Q is 50% more efficient → Q's efficiency = 1.5 × P's efficiency. If P does 1 unit/day, Q does 1.5 units/day. P's rate = 1/24/day; Q's rate = 1.5/24 = 1/16/day. Q alone takes 16 days. **Short Trick:** Q's days = P's days / efficiency ratio = 24 / 1.5 = 16.

questions.stem: A, B, and C can complete a work in 8, 12, and 24 days respectively. If A and B work on alternate days with C working every day, how many days will the work take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. C works every day; A and B alternate. Day 1 (A+C): 1/8+1/24=3/24+1/24=4/24=1/6. Day 2 (B+C): 1/12+1/24=2/24+1/24=3/24=1/8. Per 2-day cycle: 1/6+1/8=4/24+3/24=7/24. After 3 cycles (6 days): 3×7/24=21/24=7/8 done. Remaining=1/8. Day 7: A+C works at 1/6/day. Time for 1/8 = (1/8)/(1/6) = 6/8 = 3/4 day = 18 hours. Total = 6¾ days = 6 days 18 hours.

questions.stem: 20 workers finish a job in 30 days. After 10 days, 10 more workers join. In how many days is the remaining work completed?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total work = 20×30 = 600 man-days. Work done in 10 days = 20×10 = 200 man-days. Remaining = 600−200 = 400 man-days. Workers now = 20+10 = 30. Days for remaining = 400/30 = 40/3 = 13⅓ days.

questions.stem: A man and a boy together complete a work in 18 days. If the man works alone, he finishes in 24 days. How many days will the boy take alone?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Boy's rate = Combined − Man = 1/18 − 1/24. LCM(18,24)=72. = 4/72 − 3/72 = 1/72. Boy alone takes 72 days. Verify: 1/24+1/72=3/72+1/72=4/72=1/18 ✓.

questions.stem: A does ¾ of a work in 15 days. He then calls B and together they complete the remaining work in 3 days. How long would B alone take to do the whole work?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A completes ¾ of work in 15 days → A's full rate = (3/4)/15 = 1/20 per day (A alone takes 20 days). Remaining work = ¼. In 3 days with B, A does 3×(1/20) = 3/20. B does ¼−3/20 = 5/20−3/20 = 2/20 = 1/10 in 3 days → B's rate = 1/30 per day. B alone = 30 days.
